sections.html:
Lawrence County covers 613 square miles of the southwest Missouri Ozarks, and Mount Vernon is the seat. Towns include Aurora, Marionville, Miller, Pierce City, Verona, Freistatt, Halltown, Hoberg, LaRussell and Stotts City, and part of Monett lies in the county. Population was 39,401 in July 2025, up 3.7% from April 2020.

The median owner-occupied home is valued at $175,100, and 73.9% of households own. There are 16,526 housing units, and 149 building permits were issued in 2025. School, city, fire and ambulance levies depend on where a parcel sits, so know your districts before you talk numbers with a buyer.

Lawrence County is a Class 3 county run by a three-member commission. Most offices are in Mt. Vernon: the historic courthouse at 1 E. Courthouse Square, the Justice Center at 240 N. Main St., the Law Enforcement Center at 1525 Missouri Dr. and the Health Department at 1549 Missouri Dr. General questions go to the County Clerk at 1 E. Courthouse Square, Suite 101, phone 417-466-2638.

The Assessor works from the basement of the Historic Lawrence County Courthouse in Mt. Vernon. Mail goes to P.O. Box 188, Mt. Vernon, MO 65712, the phone is (417) 466-2831, and the office is open 8:00 to 4:00 on weekdays.

The Collector of Revenue is on the first floor of the courthouse at #1 Courthouse Square. Each month's collections are banked with the county treasury, which forwards them to schools, libraries, ambulance and fire districts and special road districts.

The Collector also runs the August delinquent real estate auction, issues merchant and auctioneer licenses, and handles the escrow payments that mortgage holders send for owners.

Seven countywide levies are posted on the county's website. Depending on the parcel, school, city, fire and ambulance levies come on top of them. The same page links to online payment.

Voters approved a half-cent sales tax in 2025 for the expanded Mt. Vernon Ambulance District, which is separate from the property levies.

November is mailing month, and statements should reach you by the second week. Each is due on receipt and delinquent once December 31 is over. If nothing has come by Thanksgiving, call 417-466-2410.

A missing statement never wipes out the debt or the penalty and interest that follow. Mail with a postmark after December 31 comes back unprocessed unless it includes both. Check the mailing address, the vehicles and the legal description on every statement you do receive.

  • Visit the courthouse office on weekdays from 8:00 to 3:55.
  • Mail to P.O. Box 29, Mt. Vernon, MO 65712.
  • Use the Collector's website or its phone payment line.
  • Offer cash, a personal check, a money order or a credit card.

State holidays are closed days, but the staff work through lunch. A single check can cover all of your statements, and part payments are refused. The card company keeps its own processing cost.

sections.h2: If the assessed value looks wrong
sections.html:
Phone the Assessor at (417) 466-2831 and ask for a review. A disagreement that remains goes to the county board of equalization, with filing due before the second Monday in July. After the board comes the State Tax Commission, which takes appeals up to 30 days after the date on the board's letter.

Disputing a value does not force early payment. The Commission says you may appeal first and pay afterward, or pay the whole bill by December 31 as a protest, adding a written explanation and your own estimate of market value.

LLCs, estates, trusts, corporations and limited partnerships must have an attorney file. A buyer who closed less than 30 days after the county mailed the statement can appeal directly to the Commission.

Every August the Collector offers delinquent real estate at auction. Call 417-466-2410 for the date, the parcel list and the amount that would pull yours off it.

Chapter 140 of the Revised Statutes governs these sales. The winning bidder receives a certificate, and the owner then has a redemption period to repay the amount with interest. Ask the Collector for the figure on your parcel and the length of the window.

Closing a sale first sidesteps all of it. The title company pays the Collector out of your proceeds.

Four dates matter most in Lawrence County, and a sale that straddles one of them needs a plan.

  • Second Monday in July: the last day to file with the county board of equalization.
  • August: the Collector's delinquent real estate auction.
  • November: statements are mailed and are due on receipt.
  • December 31: the postmark deadline, after which penalty and interest begin.

A house that lists in spring will usually close before the next bill exists, so the buyer inherits a bill the seller never saw. Settle in the contract who pays the current year and how it is divided, and have the title company confirm that no earlier year is open.

sections.h2: What happens at closing when tax is owed
sections.html:
The title company asks the Collector for the amount due, deducts it from your proceeds and sends the payment before it releases the balance to you. Nothing about that requires you to pay out of pocket in advance.

What can cause delay is a number that moves. Penalty and interest keep building on a delinquent bill, so a payoff taken early may be short by closing day. Ask the Collector how long a figure stays good, and have the title company refresh it near the end. If a statement never reached you, call before you list and say so; the Collector can tell you which years are paid and which are not.

Get a written payoff from the Collector, then have the Assessor confirm the acreage, address and owner of record. It is cheaper to fix a wrong parcel description before a buyer's title search catches it.

  1. Compare the vehicles and legal description on the statement with your own records.
  2. Save the paid receipt for every year you can.
  3. Agree with the buyer on how the current year splits.
  4. If any earlier year is open, confirm the August auction date.
  5. Ask the Assessor or Collector whether a relief program fits your parcel.

Selling for cash does not change the tax. The payoff still comes from the proceeds at closing, but with no buyer loan to approve, you can usually have the figure settled soon after the offer is accepted.

faqs.q: Is December 31 the Lawrence County tax deadline?
faqs.a: Yes. Statements arrive in November, and a payment postmarked after December 31 comes back unless penalty and interest are included.

faqs.q: What is the Lawrence County Collector's address?
faqs.a: The office is on the first floor of the Lawrence County Courthouse, #1 Courthouse Square, Mt. Vernon. Mail goes to P.O. Box 29, and the phone is 417-466-2410.

faqs.q: Where is the Lawrence County Assessor's office?
faqs.a: In the courthouse basement in Mt. Vernon. The phone is (417) 466-2831, and mail goes to P.O. Box 188, Mt. Vernon, MO 65712.

faqs.q: How long do I have to file a Lawrence County value appeal?
faqs.a: Until the second Monday in July for the county board. The State Tax Commission then allows 30 days from the board's letter.

faqs.q: Does the Lawrence County Collector hold a delinquent tax auction?
faqs.a: Yes, every August. Call 417-466-2410 for the date and the parcel list.
